previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted with a one-week history of productive cough and acute chest pain. He presented from dialysis with dyspnea and low-grade fever. Chest imaging revealed a new right middle lobe infiltrate concerning for pneumonia and mild pulmonary edema. He was treated with intravenous antibiotics initially, then transitioned to oral levofloxacin with clinical improvement. Chest pain, likely musculoskeletal from coughing, resolved during the stay. Troponin was mildly elevated but stable, without ECG changes, suggesting no acute coronary syndrome. He completed a scheduled hemodialysis session and remained on his baseline medications, including omeprazole for recent esophagitis. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor weight, and follow up with his outpatient team.

Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M with PMH of ESRD on HD (___), CHF, and atrial 
fibrillation  who presented with a 5 day h/o generalized 
weakness and a 1 day h/o SOB.

Acute issues

# Pulmonary edema: Exam on admission was consistent with volume 
overload and subsequent CXR showed vascular congestion and 
bilateral pulmonary edema. It was unclear at that time if this 
was due to CHF or ESRD. Patient was managed initially with 
supplemental oxygen and albuterol nebs as needed. He was taken 
to hemodialysis on morning of admission. He had 4.5 L taken off 
which resulted in complete resolution of his SOB and improvement 
in his clinical volume status. Echocardiogram obtained on ___ 
showed moderate right ventricular dysfunction with a normal LVEF 
of 60%. Patient was taken for HD again on day of discharge which 
he tolerated well. 

#Anemia: Patient reported feeling fatigued, which he attributed 
symptoms to missing scheduled transfusion. Received 1 unit pRBCs 
at HD on morning of admission with improvement in his symptoms. 
Iron studies were consistent with anemia of chronic disease. Hct 
went from 28.1 to 32.6 after transfusion and was stable at 31.3 
on discharge. Patient was evaluated by Physical Therapy. They 
recommended discharge with ___ services and home physical 
therapy.

# Atrial fibrillation/flutter: Patient's home diltiazem and 
digoxin were held on admission for bradycardia with HR in the 
___. These medications were restarted on morning of HD#2. 
Shortly after this patient was triggered for atrial flutter with 
RVR with HR up to 170s. Patient was given a one time dose of 
diltiazem 30 mg PO resulting in control of his heart rate. His 
heart rate remained stable for the rest of his time in the 
hospital. Although he has a high CHADS score, he is not 
anticoagulated presumably due to recent history of GI bleed. 

# Troponemia: Troponin found to be elevated at 0.37 but review 
of records reveals this is a stable elevation likely due to 
ESRD. CK-MB fraction was normal.  

Chronic issues

# ESRD: Secondary to diabetic nephropathy. Patient received 
scheduled HD on HD#1 and HD#3. He was continued on home 
sevelamer and cinecalcet. While in the hospital he received a 
low phosphate, low potassium diet.
 
# DM2: Hyperglycemic to 300s on admission for which patient was 
given Humalog SQ. After this patient was continued on home 
Lantus and Humalog sliding scale which resulted in stabilization 
of his blood glucose.

Transitional issues
# Patient is due for HD on ___
# Further evaluation for occult GI bleeding as cause of anemia
